record.question:
A company serves a web application through CloudFront, with an ALB forwarding requests to ECS tasks on Fargate. When the ALB returns HTTP 502, users should receive a branded error page while the HTTP response remains 502. Healthy requests must continue normally. A static HTML error page is available.

Which solution meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Store the page in a private S3 bucket. Add its REST endpoint as a CloudFront origin with origin access control, route an error-page path to that origin, and configure a custom 502 response using that page and status code 502.
Use an ALB error alarm to invoke Lambda. Have Lambda replace the application listener rule with a redirect to a public error-page URL, then restore the rule when the alarm clears.
Host the page on an S3 website endpoint. Configure Route 53 failover between the application and the website whenever an application health check fails.
Add a highest-priority ALB rule matching all request paths. Configure the rule to return a fixed 502 response containing the branded page.

explanation.text:
Option <<1>> handles the error on the request path that already serves the application. CloudFront can substitute a custom body for an origin's 502 response while retaining the 502 status. A separate cache behavior routes the error-page object to S3, and OAC permits CloudFront to read a private REST origin. Choose an error-caching TTL appropriate to recovery speed.

Option <<2>> changes routing globally after a metric alarm, so it redirects healthy requests too and requires custom rule-management logic. Option <<3>> performs DNS failover rather than substituting the body of a particular 502 response. An S3 website endpoint also cannot use OAC. Option <<4>> matches healthy requests as well and prevents them from reaching the application.

The custom response improves the user experience; it does not repair the underlying application. Keep the error page independently available, because a failure fetching it changes the response CloudFront can return.

AWS references checked on 2026-09-18:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/GeneratingCustomErrorResponses.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html

diagram_alt: Only an origin 502 invokes the custom body path, while successful responses and the 502 status retain their meaning.

sources.supports: CloudFront substitutes custom error responses and depends on error-page availability.
OAC protects an S3 REST origin and is unsupported for S3 website endpoints.

editorial_notes: Made HTTP status preservation and per-response handling explicit. Preserved key 1 and removed ambiguous browser-redirection wording.
